h1: The 5 Best Personal Small Safes of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Personal Small Safes 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five personal small safes, from mountable keypad boxes to portable travel cases, sorted by lock type, size and price tier.
summary: The Bonsaii 0.23 cu ft keypad safe with USB-C backup power is our best overall pick. Voncabay is the best for lockout protection, Yuanshikj is the best budget mountable box, and Master Lock and Amazon Basics cover portable and travel needs.
intro: A small safe fails in two quiet ways: the box walks out the door because it was never bolted down, or the owner is locked out when a battery dies. Both are avoidable if you read the spec sheet.
We ranked five personal safes on mounting, lock type, backup access and price tier. Everything below comes from the product listings, so keep the real-world caveats in mind.

products.name: Bonsaii Small Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Valuables, 0.23 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: A mountable steel box with a USB-C emergency power option.
products.description:
The Bonsaii is a 0.23 cu ft mountable steel security box with an electronic keypad. It lists pre-drilled installation holes and a USB-C emergency power backup, and sits in the $25-50 bucket.

It ranks above the Voncabay because the USB-C backup solves the worst keypad-safe problem, a dead battery. The Voncabay answers with a low-battery warning instead, which is helpful but not a rescue.

Buy it for a bedroom or desk drawer where you can bolt it down. The caveat is size: 0.23 cu ft holds documents and small items, not a laptop.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants a bolt-down keypad safe with a lockout rescue.
products.skipIf: You need to store bulky items.

products.name: Voncabay Money Safe Box for Home with Digital Keypad, 0.23 Cu. Ft., Black
products.verdict: Smart guardrails: interior light, battery warning and a wrong-code lockout.
products.description:
The Voncabay is a 0.23 cu ft mountable steel box in the $25-50 bucket. It adds an automatic interior light, a low-battery warning and a five minute lockout after three wrong entries.

It sits just below the Bonsaii because it warns you about the battery rather than offering a USB-C way back in. The lockout makes guessing codes slower, which the Bonsaii listing does not mention.

It suits households where kids or guests might poke at the keypad. The caveat is the same small interior.
products.idealFor: Homes with curious kids or frequent guests.
products.skipIf: You want an emergency power port.

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: The cheapest mountable box here, with two steel locking bolts.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj is a 0.2 cu ft steel box with dual steel locking bolts and a magnetic auto-lock door. Mounting bolts and pre-drilled holes are included, and it sits in the under $25 bucket.

It ranks third because it lacks the extras of the two above, namely no USB-C power and no lockout feature in its listing. In exchange it costs a tier less.

Buy it for a first safe or a dorm drawer. The compromise is fewer conveniences, so keep the included key somewhere safe.
products.skipIf: You want battery warnings or backup power.

products.name: Master Lock Small Travel Safe with Cable, Gray Combination Lock Box, 5900D
products.verdict: A tethered combination box for hotels, cars and gym bags.
products.description:
This Master Lock travel safe has a 4-digit combination with no key to lose. It adds a tether cable, a charging cable access port and water resistance, in the under $25 bucket.

It ranks below the mountable boxes because a tether is easier to defeat than a bolted steel box. It wins on portability, which the bolt-down models cannot offer.

Buy it for trips, where you can loop the cable around a fixed object. Treat it as a deterrent, not a vault.
products.idealFor: Travelers who want a locking box for hotels and cars.
products.skipIf: You need a fixed home safe.

products.name: Amazon Basics Portable Security Case Lock Box Safe with Combination Lock
products.verdict: An anti-pry steel case with a foam-padded interior.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics case is portable with anti-pry steel construction, a foam-padded interior and a zinc alloy combination lock. Its price tier is under $25.

Bottom spot comes down to one gap: it has no tether or mounting option listed, so it is only as secure as where you store it. The padded interior is its edge over the Master Lock for fragile items.

Buy it for documents and small electronics you want protected. It is a deterrent more than a safe.
products.idealFor: Protecting fragile items on the move.
products.skipIf: You want to anchor it down.

whatMatters.detail: A safe that is not fixed to something can be carried off whole. Mountable models ship with holes in the base or back, and some include bolts. Check the listing for mounting hardware or pre-drilled holes before relying on one.
Keypad safes run on batteries, and a dead battery can lock you out. A USB-C emergency port or a physical key gives you a way in. Look for these in the feature bullets.
A 0.23 cu ft box holds papers, passports and small items, not a laptop. Size is easy to overestimate from photos. Read the cu ft figure or the dimensions in the listing.
Combination dials need no battery but are slower, while keypads are quick and can add lockouts. Pick the type that matches how often you open it. The listing states which lock the safe uses.

Travel cases move with you and rely on a tether, while mounted safes stay put and resist theft better. Decide where the safe will live first. The listing usually says portable or mountable in the title.

faq.a: Their listings do not claim fire protection, so we do not rate them for it. Treat them as theft deterrents.

faq.q: Should I bolt a small safe down?
faq.a: Yes. An unbolted small safe can be carried away, so use the pre-drilled holes on the Bonsaii, Voncabay or Yuanshikj.

faq.q: Is the Bonsaii worth it over the Yuanshikj?
faq.a: If a dead battery worries you, yes, because of the USB-C backup. Otherwise the cheaper Yuanshikj has the same basic size.

faq.q: Can a travel safe replace a home safe?
faq.a: Not really. A tether is a deterrent, while a bolted steel box offers more resistance.
Change batteries on time and keep the spare key or emergency access somewhere separate.
Not in the 0.23 cu ft boxes. Those hold documents and small items.

finalTake: The Bonsaii is the safest default for most homes, mainly for its USB-C backup. Choose the Voncabay when lockouts matter and the Yuanshikj when budget does. For trips, the Master Lock travel safe is the practical choice, with the Amazon Basics case as a padded alternative.
